title: traffic-partitioning-strategies-and-ops-checklist-wip
content:
Purpose
This is a working doc for engineers, product managers, SREs and data teams to align on traffic partitioning strategies and operational checklists for gradual rollouts, canaries, and A/B experiments. Focus: safe traffic slicing, clear telemetry contracts, and an actionable ops checklist for launch day and rapid mitigation.

TL;DR summary
- Prefer deterministic slices (user cohorts or API key groups) for early canaries; move to random percentage slices for broader AB tests.
- Define a small set of primary metrics (latency, error rate, quality) and a clear abort/scale-up policy with numeric thresholds.
- Automate guardrails for fast cutover: traffic re-route API + fallback model chain + capacity buffer.
- Runbook + checklist below is optimized for the Console rollout controls; adapt for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Key definitions (context for cross-functional readers)
- Canary: a narrow, targeted slice (e.g., 0.5–5% traffic) to validate service/infra characteristics.
- Experiment (A/B): randomized split to measure product/quality impact at scale.
- Slice: any deterministic group of requests (by user_id, org_id, route, api_key) used to partition traffic.
- Telemetry contract: exact metrics, latency windows, and data retention necessary for decisioning.

When to use which strategy
- Smoke/Infra Canary: use deterministic internal cohorts (internal users, org IDs, telemetry-only keys). Keep slice tiny (0.1–1%). Goal: catch infra regressions and regressions in throttling, KV cache behavior.
- Customer Canary: small percentage (1–5%) of live customers selected by risk profile. Goal: detect behavioral regressions and customer-visible issues.
- Product A/B: randomized slices at 5–50% per variant depending on signal strength and cost. Goal: measure quality and business metrics.

Slice sizing guidance (practical rules)
- 0.1–1%: infra smoke for runtime and kernel regressions (fast fail, very low exposure).
- 1–5%: customer canary to detect production-only failures and edge-case prompts.
- 5–20%: early product experiments where quality signals are noisy and cost is moderate.
- 20–50%: mature feature experiments with monitoring in alignment across eng/product/SRE.
- >50%: near-global rollout, requires full runbook and stakeholder signoff.

Telemetry contract (must be in place before traffic is cut)
- Primary metrics (per-slice, per-model): p50 latency (ms), p95 latency (ms), error rate (% requests with 5xx or malformed responses), token-usage per request (avg), and API-level cost estimator (USD/1k tokens).
- Quality metrics (sampled): human-evaluated prompt quality (weekly), automatic regression checks (BLEU/ROUGE-like or eval prompts), hallucination signal rate (as defined by eval suite).
- Business metrics (if product experiment): conversion rate, retention delta, upsell signal.
- Windows and retention: compute p50/p95 over 1m, 5m, 1h windows. Retain raw traces for at least 7 days for root cause.

Abort and escalation thresholds (starter defaults — tune per product)
- Immediate abort if error rate increases by >1.5x absolute or crosses 2.0% over baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Immediate abort if p95 latency degrades by >2x relative to baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Cost spike: if token cost per successful request increases >3x and no degradation in quality, trigger review and potential rollback.
- Quality regression (human or automated) exceeding 5% relative degradation across sampled prompts over 24h -> pause rollout and investigate.

Operational automation and fail-safe primitives
- Traffic reroute API: single call to move all traffic to fallback variant or previous model version. Must be executable by SRE and product on-call.
- Fallback chain: model variant A -> variant B (cheaper/older quantized) -> synthetic response policy (if configured).
- Capacity buffer: reserve +20% capacity for canary bursts; autoscaling cooldowns shortened for initial 30 minutes post-cut.
- Canary TTL: automatic rollback to 0% after N minutes if no one manually extends (default N=120).

Role responsibilities (cross-functional)
- Engineering (serving/runtime): implement slice selection, traffic re-route endpoints, throttling behavior.
- Product: specify experiment hypothesis, primary + guardrail metrics, traffic targets.
- SRE/Oncall: validate infra readiness, run runbook, execute emergency cutovers.
- Data Science/Analysis: define statistical significance thresholds, run posterior analysis and provide confidence intervals.
- Solutions/CS: prepare customer-facing comms for customer canary or partner experiments.

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before traffic change)
- [ ] Experiment config reviewed and in Git (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Telemetry contract validated end-to-end: dashboards populated, alerts wired to oncall.
- [ ] Load test for autoscaling with synthetic traffic at expected canary QPS + 20%.
- [ ] Safety net policies configured (abort thresholds, TTL, reroute API key access).
- [ ] Owners and escalation matrix documented in the runbook and calendar invites created for launch window.
- [ ] Sampled output pipeline enabled and reviewers assigned for manual quality checks.

Launch day runbook (timeline and quick actions)
- T-30m: final go/no-go sync (Eng, Product, SRE, DS). Confirm dashboards ready.
- T-0: enable canary slice (0.5–1%). Note timestamp and change ID.
- T+5m: sanity check for 1m/5m windows; verify no immediate infra regressions.
- T+15m: expanded telemetry check; if stable, increase to next defined percent (e.g., 3–5%).
- T+60–120m: if signals stable and quality checks pass, proceed to AB or broader percent as defined.
- Any time: if abort thresholds hit -> execute immediate rollback, notify stakeholders, open incident, collect traces.

Emergency rollback steps (engineer-friendly)
1) Execute traffic reroute to previous stable variant (API call example in repo PR).
2) Disable experiment flags and set TTL to zero to prevent re-enablement.
3) If model runtime is causing infra overload, scale down worker concurrency or disable batching features temporarily.
4) Gather traces (trace IDs, sample request IDs) and assign to incident owner.
5) Communicate via #prod-rollouts channel and notify customers if customer-facing.

Post-launch evaluation windows and decisions
- Short window (first 24h): safety-first — ensure no safety metrics tripped, collect early quality samples.
- Medium window (3–7 days): analyze product/quality deltas; if stable, move to scaled rollout.
- Long window (2–4 weeks): business metrics converge; prepare final decision to promote or rollback.

Experiment config template (minimal fields)
- name: short-name-of-experiment
- owner: eng/product owner
- start_time: RFC3339
- slices: { type: cohort|random|route, selector: string, percentages: [0.5, 5, ...] }
- metrics: [primary_metric_keys]
- abort_thresholds: {metric: value, window: minutes}
- fallback: variant_id
- monitoring_dashboards: [list of dashboard ids]
- contact_list: [pager, slack channel, escalation matrix]
(we keep this in the config repo as a YAML in infra/experiment-configs)

Notes on observability and dashboard design
- Dashboards should have per-slice breakdowns and a global view. Avoid dashboards that aggregate away slice-level signals.
- Surface absolute counts first (requests/min) to avoid over-reacting to noisy ratios at low volumes.
- Include a side-by-side model-variant comparison panel for p95 and error rate.
- Add a sampled output viewer storing 1 in N responses with request metadata for quick triage.

Sampling, privacy and sensitive data handling
- Sampled payloads must be redacted for PII by default; use the redaction library in infra before storing to S3.
- For Private deployments, ensure sampled outputs remain in customer-owned buckets and follow contract.

Open questions and action items
- Q: Should the initial canary TTL default to 60 or 120 minutes? Proposal: 120 by default; shorter for infra-only smoke. (Action: @Priya to finalize by 2025-03-05)
- Q: Do we allow dynamic slice sizes driven by ML-based progression policy? Risk: risky for auditability. (Action: @Samir to prototype and present tradeoffs)
- Need a small CLI tool for one-click rollback and status check (Action: @Diego to draft an RFC).

Appendix: example minimal rollout timeline for a model variant A -> B
- Day 0: internal smoke with 0.1% internal keys for 30m.
- Day 1: customer canary 1% for 2h, expand to 5% if stable.
- Day 2–4: AB test at 10%/10% for statistical signals + manual quality checks.
- Day 7: decide promote/rollback based on product/quality/business metrics.

Next steps (near term)
- Convert this doc into a Confluence page and link to experiment config repo (owner: Maya).
- Add the config template to infra/experiment-configs and create a simple GitHub Action to validate metrics listed.
- Schedule a cross-functional rehearsal for the rollout runbook (target week of 2025-03-17).

If you edit this doc: keep the telemetry contract and abort thresholds explicit. Small wording tweaks are fine; major threshold changes need cross-functional signoff.
